⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino.
  • Recent findings suggest that juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches.
  • According to recent reports, that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Recent findings suggest that juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

According to recent reports, that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the newly introduced refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

Recent findings suggest that the wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

Industry observers note that the trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

The contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

The case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Industry observers note that luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

The run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

According to recent reports, the schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

Sources indicate that the first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

Chelsea are continuing to assess their attacking options as they look to build a squad capable of competing for major honours, with the club reportedly keeping tabs on one of Europe’s most exciting young strikers.

Club Brugge forward Nicolo Tresoldi has attracted growing attention following his remarkable goalscoring form, with Chelsea among several Premier League clubs monitoring the German international ahead of a potential future transfer.

According to TEAMtalk, Chelsea and Manchester City sent representatives to watch Tresoldi score a hat-trick for Club Brugge, while Arsenal, Tottenham and Newcastle also had scouts present.

The 22-year-old has enjoyed an impressive run in Belgium, with his recent performances strengthening his reputation as a promising attacking talent. Chelsea are assessing their options in central attack as they continue planning for the future.

Industry observers note that however, the Blues face a significant challenge if they decide to pursue a deal. Club Brugge are reportedly unwilling to sell Tresoldi in January and would demand a club-record transfer fee to sanction his departure.

That valuation is expected to exceed the €40 million the Belgian club received for Christos Tzolis, meaning any potential deal could require a substantial financial commitment.

Tresoldi could be an attractive long-term addition to Chelsea’s attack, but the club will need to weigh his potential against the competition for his signature.

With several Premier League rivals monitoring the striker and Club Brugge determined to keep him beyond January, a summer transfer battle could develop if his impressive form continues.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 22:35, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 22:37.
  • Fulham goalkeeper Benjamin Lecomte will miss the rest of the 2026-27 season with an Achilles injury.
  • The Frenchman sustained the injury in a behind-closed-doors game against West Ham United during the international break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 22:35, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 22:37.

Fulham goalkeeper Benjamin Lecomte will miss the rest of the 2026-27 season with an Achilles injury.

The Frenchman sustained the injury in a behind-closed-doors game against West Ham United during the international break.

Revealing the extent of the injury, Alvaro Arbeloa told reporters on Friday: "Unfortunately, Lecomte injured his Achilles tendon against West Ham, so he will be out for the rest of the season.

“We are sorry for him because he is very notable and it was very sad.”.

Lecomte has not played in the Premier League this season, but he featured in three of Fulham’s EFL Cup games, including a 1-0 defeat to Crystal Palace last month.

As a result of Lecomte’s injury, Alex Borto and Dino Kaiser will be the backup options for the club’s undisputed first-choice goalkeeper Bernd Leno.

Arbeloa also revealed Emile Smith Rowe is unlikely to be fit for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off against Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium.

“Smith Rowe, he has some pain in his hip, so I think he won't be available for tomorrow.

“I think it’s nothing serious - some pain and discomfort, so we will see next week, but it doesn't look really serious.”.

The news of Smith Rowe's physical issue represents the latest setback in what is proving to be a difficult campaign for the Arsenal academy product.

The 28-year-old made 37 Premier League appearances in Marco Silva's final season in charge, but he has featured in just four league games under Arbeloa due to injury and selection decisions.

In more positive news, Arbeloa explained that Tom Cairney could be in contention to return to the squad after missing the draw against Newcastle United before the international window.

If available, Cairney could have a role to play off the bench as Fulham look to end their woeful run of form against Manchester City.

The Cottagers have lost each of their last 17 Premier League games against the Citizens since they played out a 2-2 draw at Craven Cottage in September 2011.

Meanwhile, their last head-to-head victory took place in April 2009 when Clinton Dempsey netted a brace in a 3-1 win at the Etihad Stadium.

Henry Pollock was at the centre of an East Midlands derby flare-up that sparked a second-half Leicester onslaught as Northampton were overpowered at a sodden Mattioli Woods Welford Road.

Pollock, withdrawn after 52 minutes, may wish to reflect on the wisdom of riling the Tigers in their own lair.

“That was a proper Tigers second half and a really pleasing performance,” Geoff Parling, their director of rugby, noted.

According to recent reports, “We got on the front foot and highlighted our power. The way the guys problem-solved was brilliant and I’m just really pleased with the emotional energy they threw into that game.

“The way we were physically for each other – I’m really pleased.

“The challenge for us, if we want to be a title-winning team, is to play like that when it isn’t Northampton Saints. We have to play with that heart – the fire we demonstrated in our chests – but also the calmness we showed too.

“I think if we play our game to the best of our ability we can knock over anyone.”.

It’s a big day for Alex Coles, who celebrates his milestone 150th cap today.

The 27-year-old lock follows Fraser Dingwall, Rory Hutchinson and Alex Mitchell to become the fourth member of Saints’ current squad to reach 150 appearances for his boyhood club, eight years after making his debut in 2018.

Coles marks one of nine changes to Saints’ side for the Derby Day clash, with Emmanuel Iyogun, Curtis Langdon, Ed Prowse, Tom Pearson and Henry Pollock the other names coming into the forward pack.

Cleopas Kundiona retains his place in the front row while milestone man Coles joins Prowse in the second row against Tigers.

Josh Kemeny, with the 27-year-old continues at blindside flanker while Tom Pearson is set to make his first Prem appearance of the season.

Northampton Saints: J Pater; T Freeman, R Hutchinson, F Dingwall, G Hendy; F Smith, A Mitchell, E Iyogun, C Langdon, C Kundiona, A Coles, E Prowse, J Kemeny, T Pearson, H Pollock.

Replacements: R Smith, D Fischetti, I Neculai, JJ Van Der Mescht, T Lockett, C Chick, A McParland, O Sleightholme.

Parling has made five changes from the side that endured a 41-17 defeat to Pau.

Solomone Kata returns from injury to start at inside centre, with Gabriel Hamer-Webb and Jack van Poortvliet also coming into the backline to replace Ollie Hassell-Collins and Tom Whiteley respectively.

In the pack, Joe Heyes joins Archie van der Flier and Jamie Blamire who retain their places in the front row, while the second row make up of Cameron Henderson and Ollie Chessum remains unchanged.

Aaron Wainwright comes back into the starting lineup in the back row, with Finn Carnduff moving to openside flanker, with Olly Cracknell going at No 8.

Leicester: F Steward; A Radwan, W Wand, S Kata; G Hamer-Webb; B Searle, J van Poortvliet; A van der Flier, J Blamire, J Heyes, C Henderson, O Chessum, A Wainwright, F Carnduff, O Cracknell.

Replacements:  R Asiata, T Haffar, W Hurd, J Thompson, J Moro, T Whiteley, O Bailey, G Pearson.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of Leicester Tigers v Northampton Saints.

The Prem’s derby weekend continues today at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, where Geoff Parling’s side go head-to-head in with their East Midlands rivals.

Both Leicester and Northampton have two wins from the opening three rounds of the season and with both sides involved in a number of high-scoring encounters already in the fresh campaign, we could be in for a real treat.

According to recent reports, tigers started the season with a 38-40 loss at home to Saracens, but bounced back promptly with wins over Gloucester and Newcastle Red Bulls. They will be itching to right a few wrongs after suffering a chastening Champions Cup defeat in Pau last week.

Northampton, meanwhile, have notched up wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Bath either side of loss to Bristol Bears.

A win today for Saints would be their first on the road since defeating Exeter Chiefs at Sandy Park in April.

“It (the East Midlands derby) means a lot to everyone, we know it will be a great atmosphere at Mattioli Woods Welford Road,” mentioned Parling.

“I don’t think with this sort of game either team has to build it up too much emotionally because that just comes, so I think it’s actually about being really really calm in the moment.”.

“Hopefully we can put the best of ourselves out there and I’m sure Saints will be able to do exactly the same.”.

Saints are without a victory in Leicester since January 2023, when a single point decided the 18-19 result.

Since then, the last five meetings between the sides have been won by the hosts on the day – with Saints last taking home the bragging rights when a Tom Litchfield hat-trick helped Northampton to a 45-31 win on home soil in last season’s league play-off.

According to recent reports, kick-off gets underway at 3.05pm. Stay with us here for all the latest updates.

Everton could look to make a major statement in the January transfer window as David Moyes considers ways to strengthen his side’s attacking options.

After concerns over the team’s lack of goals, the Toffees are reportedly exploring a move for a forward with proven Premier League experience.

Manchester United’s Marcus Rashford has emerged as a potential target, with reports suggesting Everton are discussing the possibility of bringing the England international to Merseyside.

A deal would give Moyes another versatile attacking option, although several key details would need to be resolved before a transfer could progress.

According to Football Insider, former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness believes a move for Rashford is being discussed seriously ahead of the January window.

Speaking on Football Insider’s Inside Track podcast, Wyness said: “Yes, this is definitely being talked about and quite strongly. And I think that could be an interesting solution.”.

The former Everton chief executive also pointed to Rashford’s previous loan spells and suggested that a move closer to Manchester could benefit the player.

“Rashford did well when he was on loan at Villa and at Barcelona as well. I think it could work, and I think being close to where he is in Manchester, just along the M63, could also benefit him greatly as well,” Wyness explained.

Industry observers note that the comments suggest that a January switch is a possibility worth monitoring, although neither club has confirmed an agreement. Separate reporting from FootballTransfers has also indicated that Everton and Manchester United have held early discussions over a potential winter move.

Wyness drew comparisons with Jack Grealish, who has made an impact at Everton when available, adding: “We’ve seen Jack (Grealish) moving across that way as well, and when he’s fit, Jack is certainly a big asset for Everton. So I think Rashford would be a very interesting signing, and I’m hearing there’s a lot of smoke here; it’s definitely being discussed.”.

He then added: “I wouldn’t be surprised to see something happening in January.”.

Industry observers note that for Everton, Rashford’s versatility could be a major attraction. Although he has often operated from the left, he can also play centrally, potentially giving Moyes additional options across the frontline. His arrival could provide support for Thierno Barry and help address the team’s need for more goals.

However, the financial structure of any deal would be crucial. Everton would need to consider Rashford’s wages, Manchester United’s valuation and whether a permanent transfer or loan arrangement would be realistic. The forward’s willingness to join another Premier League club would also be a significant factor.

Rashford could represent an ambitious addition for Everton if the club can find an agreement that works financially. His Premier League experience and ability to operate in several attacking positions would give Moyes greater flexibility, while a change of environment could offer the player a fresh start.

Sources indicate that the comparison with Grealish is particularly relevant to Everton’s approach. The club could look to provide Rashford with an environment in which he can rebuild his confidence and contribute more consistently, although any potential success would depend on his fitness, form and role within the team.

Nevertheless, a transfer is far from guaranteed. The reported discussions remain at an early stage, and Everton must still resolve the financial details and establish whether Rashford would be open to the move.

For now, Wyness’s comments add weight to speculation surrounding Everton’s January intends. If negotiations progress, Rashford could become a name to watch as Moyes looks to strengthen his attacking options for the second half of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that arriving in Cannes at just 15 years old, Zinedine Zidane helped write one of the most beautiful pages in the history of the Riviera club thanks to the fourth place achieved in the spring of 1991. Alas, the following season turned into a disaster between elimination in the round of 16 in the UEFA Cup and above all a descent to the second division. A relegation that looks like a godsend for the Girondins de Bordeaux as told to The Team its president at the time, Alain Afflelou.

“He had just turned 20. I had seen him two, three times briefly on Téléfoot. I find myself at the end of the 1992 season with Alain Pedretti, the president of Cannes who was going down to D2 while we were moving up with the Girondins, he explained. He needed to downsize because he had a large payroll. I needed to place players because we had a substantial squad. We make exchanges. ».

Recent findings suggest that among the most promising players of his generation, Zinedine Zidane inevitably arouses envy, particularly at Olympique de Marseille where Bernard Tapie holds him in very high esteem. However, the former Marseille president never called the native of Castellane and explained in 2016 that this failure constituted “the great regret of my life as president”. The way is therefore clear for the scapular club.

According to recent reports, “Pedretti took Philippe Raschke, Rainer Ernst and Patrice Lestage from me. I had negotiated Éric Guérit and Jean-François Daniel. And I remarked to him: ‘What are you doing with little Zidane? I saw in L’Équipe that Marseille and Tapie had offered you 8 million francs. He tells me it’s bullshit, continued Alain Afflelou. ‘How much do you want?’ He blurted out to me: ‘5 million francs’. » ».

Bordeaux is preparing to do a huge deal. But as a wise businessman, Alain Afflelou is still negotiating to reduce the bill. “I am with Rolland (Courbis), my trainer. He kneed me under the table. I say it’s way too much. With Courbis, we made Pagnol! He blurted out: ‘Perhaps we can make an effort. I feel this boy has a future.’ They looked like two crooks! We took Guérit, Daniel and Zidane for 5 million while valuing Zizou at 3.5 million! “, he revealed.

Tech Report: Liverpool vs. Man Utd trophies: Who has won more honours?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1246 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Barney Corkhill | 20 Nov 2026 23:32.
  • Recent findings suggest that liverpool have won more major trophies than Manchester United, leading the Liverpool vs.
  • With a margin that small, the answer depends on what you count, because leaving out the one-off 1986 Football League Super Cup puts the clubs level, while leaving out the Community Shield gives the Reds a clear lead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Barney Corkhill | 20 Nov 2026 23:32.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool have won more major trophies than Manchester United, leading the Liverpool vs. Man Utd trophies count 69-68 on every senior competitive honour as of November 20, 2026.

With a margin that small, the answer depends on what you count, because leaving out the one-off 1986 Football League Super Cup puts the clubs level, while leaving out the Community Shield gives the Reds a clear lead.

Neither club has lifted a trophy since Liverpool's 2024-25 Premier League title, which nudged the Anfield outfit back ahead of their eternal rivals.

Liverpool and Manchester United share the record for English league titles with 20 each, after the Merseysiders' 2024-25 Premier League win matched the total the Red Devils reached in 2012-13.

United are stronger in the FA Cup, with 13 wins to Liverpool's eight, and in the Community Shield, which they have won or shared 21 times against 16 for the Anfield club.

Liverpool hold the record of 10 League Cups, four more than their rivals, and they are the only one of the pair to have won the Football League Super Cup, which was played only once.

The gap opens up in Europe, where six European Cups, three UEFA Cups and four UEFA Super Cups give the Reds 13 continental trophies to United's six.

Liverpool have more trophies than Manchester United on the fullest count, one ahead, and they also lead when Community Shields are left out.

United only draw level if the 1986 Football League Super Cup is removed or shared Community Shields are discounted, and they only go ahead on a count limited to the league, FA Cup and League Cup, which they lead 39-38.

That makes the Reds the more decorated club, since they lead or are level on every method that includes European competition, and the only count that favours the Old Trafford side ignores continental silverware altogether.

United's honours board leaves out the Super Cup and so highlights the rivals level, which is a fair reading, but even on that basis the Red Devils still need one more trophy to go ahead.

Opinion is split on whether the Community Shield should count as a genuine trophy, and the FA itself treats it as a friendly for disciplinary purposes, so bookings in it do not carry over into other domestic games.

The fixture has only been contested between the league champions and the FA Cup winners since 1974, and before that it was an invitational match.

Seven of United's Community Shields and three of Liverpool's came before that change, which strengthens the case for leaving the trophy out.

The Anfield club's own honours page lists 52 major men's honours, a figure that excludes both the Community Shield and the Football League Super Cup, and the Community Shield never appeared on the honours board at their old Melwood training ground either.

Counting the Football League Super Cup but not the Community Shield gives the Reds a 53-47 lead, a six-trophy cushion over the Red Devils.

The Football League Super Cup was set up after the Heysel Stadium disaster in May 1985 and the European ban on English clubs that followed, as a replacement competition for the six sides who would have played on the continent in 1985-86.

Liverpool beat Everton in a two-legged final held back until September 1986, winning 3-1 at Anfield and 4-1 at Goodison Park for a 7-2 aggregate victory.

The tournament was never played again, which is why some honours boards ignore it, and counting it or not decides whether the Merseysiders lead or the clubs are level.

A drawn Community Shield used to be shared, and Liverpool's list includes five shared editions (1964, 1965, 1977, 1986 and 1990), while United shared four (1965, 1967, 1977 and 1990).

The years 1965, 1977 and 1990 appear on both lists, and removing every shared Community Shield leaves both clubs on 64, another count where Man United can claim a tie but not a lead.

Manchester United have their strongest case at home, with 60 domestic honours to Liverpool's 55 when Community Shields and the Football League Super Cup are counted.

In the three main domestic competitions, the league, FA Cup and League Cup, the Red Devils lead 39-38 thanks to five more FA Cup wins.

Cup finals between the pair have been split evenly, as United won the 1977 FA Cup final 2-1 and the 1996 final 1-0, while the Reds won the League Cup finals of 1983 and 2003.

The 1983 final went to extra time, with Alan Kennedy and Ronnie Whelan cancelling out Norman Whiteside's opener for a 2-1 win, and Steven Gerrard and Michael Owen scored in the 2-0 win in Cardiff 20 years later.

For every result between the two clubs rather than just the silverware, our Man Utd vs. Liverpool head-to-head record covers each meeting.

Liverpool's six European Cups are more than any other British team has won and double United's three, and that record is what separates the clubs.

The Reds add three UEFA Cups and four UEFA Super Cups, while United's six European trophies are completed by a Europa League, a Cup Winners' Cup and one UEFA Super Cup.

United edge the world honours 2-1, having won the 1999 Intercontinental Cup and the 2008 Club World Cup, while the Merseysiders won the Club World Cup in 2019.

For the stories behind several of those European nights, including the 2005 final in Istanbul, our rundown of Liverpool's 10 greatest comebacks goes back through the club's most dramatic recoveries.

Manchester United's modern haul was built under Sir Alex Ferguson, who won 38 trophies in 26 years in charge between 1986 and 2013, including 13 league titles, five FA Cups and two Champions League titles.

The teams behind that run feature heavily in our ranking of Manchester United's 10 greatest ever teams, which sets the Ferguson sides against the club's earlier eras.

The latest swings came in 2023-24, when Liverpool's League Cup win put them one ahead on the full count before the Red Devils beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final to draw level again.

The Reds' 2024-25 Premier League title then put them one clear, while on the count that ignores the Super Cup the same sequence went from a tie to a United lead and back to the current tie.

Liverpool and Manchester United are both in the 2026-27 Champions League league phase, so Europe offers the biggest single swing, alongside the FA Cup, the League Cup and the next Community Shield.

One trophy for United without a reply from Anfield would level the full count, while any Liverpool success would stretch the gap to two.

Liverpool appear to have a better chance of adding to their haul in the 2026-27 campaign, with Man United out of the League Cup and having seen any faint hopes of a title challenge evaporate amidst their worst-ever start to a Premier League season.

The Old Trafford side are now led by Mauricio Pochettino, who became head coach in November 2026 after Michael Carrick was sacked.

To see what the newly introduced head coach brings, our breakdown of Pochettino's record against every Premier League club shows how his past teams have fared against each top-flight side.

For a view of current strength rather than history, our ranking of the best football teams in the world highlights where Liverpool sit among Europe's elite.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has admitted he has "no idea" about whether he will be at Anfield beyond the end of the season.

Van Dijk has established himself as a Liverpool icon in his 389 appearances since joining the club from Southampton in 2018.

The Dutchman has helped the Merseyside club win numerous pieces of silverware, including two Premier League titles and the 2018-19 Champions League.

However, it is unclear how much longer he will play a part in Liverpool's quest for trophies, with his current contract set to expire at the end of the campaign.

Van Dijk recently commented on his situation while on international duty, insisting that he is "not in any panic" over his Anfield future.

The centre-back has reiterated his relaxed outlook in an interview with Sky Sports, in which he conceded he has "no idea" whether he will sign a new Liverpool deal.

"The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion," Van Dijk mentioned.

"Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

"At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.

"But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game.

"Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the fresh year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a substantial part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.

Sources indicate that "If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer.".

At the age of 35, Van Dijk remains an integral part of the Liverpool squad, demonstrated by the fact he has played every minute of the club's 10 Premier League matches this term.

Van Dijk is now preparing to make his 350th Premier League appearance in Sunday's highly anticipated clash against rivals Manchester United.

The Netherlands international has made 282 of his 349 top-flight appearances in a Liverpool shirt after featuring in 67 Premier League matches for Southampton.

Van Dijk will hope to mark his milestone outing with a victory, although he only won seven of his previous 18 Premier League matches against Man United (D5, L6).

  • It has been revealed that “I am very grateful for the support received.
  • “Against Arsenal, I was transparent about what happened: I was simply sick and maybe I didn’t listen to my body enough.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On October 23, two days after the draw conceded in the Champions League against Arsenal (2-2), Bayern Munich revealed the emergency hospitalization of its coach Vincent Kompany. The 40-year-old Belgian was attending reserve team training at the Bavarian club’s training center when he felt unwell. Victim of a dislocated shoulder in his fall, the former Manchester City defender ultimately remained away from the field for four weeks due to meningitis. This morning, he made his comeback in front of the media, on the eve of the reception in Cologne, as part of the 10th day of the Bundesliga.

It has been revealed that “I am very grateful for the support received. It was an intense period. At the time, it was a unique experience. Looking back, everything worked out perfectly. I immediately received support from the club and the doctors. I am very grateful for that. We try to promptly regain our composure and wait for the results. Everything went well; all tests were positive. I must say that I am in great shape. We have had numerous tests, all of which were conclusive. In this moment of serenity, we also try to learn. I also found it fascinating to observe the team from another angle, to see how the players and staff work. Now I feel great again and I’m happy to be back with the team.”he declared, before explaining that he did not know how to listen to his body just after the C1 shock against the Gunners.

“Against Arsenal, I was transparent about what happened: I was simply sick and maybe I didn’t listen to my body enough. Everything that followed flowed from that. I don’t want to minimize the facts, it was a shock. But it was the consequence of my perseverance when I needed a break. Now I feel good, I’ve been through a long process since then. I hope the situation returns to normal as soon as possible. I am infinitely grateful for the reaction of the club and all the medical staff, who were there day and night. They went out of their way to help me. I would also like to thank my staff, who persevered and allowed us to draw strength during this difficult period. I loved the match against Atlético. It was one of the most memorable moments of my coaching career, even though I wasn’t there. We will remember this memory, and it will give us strength for the future. ».

Finally, at a time when current football displays a very busy schedule and ever-increasing pressure, Kompany responded to doubts about his state of health. Is the Belgian sufficiently armed to withstand the shock at the head of a club like Bayern? For the main person concerned, what happened to him is not due to the status of the club he coaches. “I understand the questions that will arise. The truth is that we always tend to overthink when we don’t have all the information. We are undefeated and I took the longest vacation of my life. As a manager, I can’t say there is more pressure than at Burnley in the Championship. It can happen to anyone, and we can learn from it. » The message got through.

Neymar's streak of rage continued this week as he erupted with an expletive rant at rival fans who were provoking him.

The Santos star, 34, raised hell at Coritiba fans following his side's 1-0 win over them on Wednesday, with the climax of the Brazilian season approaching.

'Don't f*** around! You're going to Serie B, you idiots,' he shouted.

It has been revealed that 'Suck it! You have to respect me, respect me, you f****** small team.'.

It had been a frustrating day in fairness - Santos' team bus had broken down on the way, requiring the squad to change vehicles.

And this is not the first time Neymar has vented his spleen this season.

Neymar branded Coritiba a 'small f****** team' in a rant at rival supporters who taunted him.

Earlier this season, he was involved in a furious altercation with rival officials in the tunnel.

In August, he was involved in a furious altercation with Remo officials after Santos beat them in the last 16 of the Brazilian Cup.

The Brazilian football icon screamed inside the tunnel as he was drawn into a heated exchange with Remo's directors.

He repeatedly shouted the word 'eliminated' before taunting the rivals with a series of gestures at his dressing room's entrance.

Despite his bragging over other teams, it has been a distinctly average campaign for Santos so far.

Santos sit eighth in the Brazilian Serie A and, despite him telling Coritiba that they will go down, that looks unlikely with the southern side sat 13th out of 20 with four games to go, four points above the drop zone.

Meanwhile, while he mocked Remo over being eliminated from the cup, Santos went out in the quarter-finals 3-0 on aggregate to Palmeiras.

Neymar has had a fairly effective season personally, scoring 10 goals and recording eight assists in all competitions while captaining Santos.

It remains to be seen whether he will play beyond the end of his contract in December, but the club's chief executive, who happens to be Neymar's dad, certainly wants to extend his son's term.

'We know that in every transfer window, offers come in for him to leave. Yet Neymar always chooses to stay at Santos. What I'm anticipating is that, first and foremost, I need to keep Neymar happy. Do you understand?' he said.

'And if he's happy here, I can keep him here. So, look, down this final stretch, the work we've done to structure the squad and open up positive possibilities has given us the license to dream.'.

Neymar, who was widely regarded as one of the greatest footballers of his generation during his time at Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, returned to his boyhood club Santos from Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal in January 2025.

His £200million move from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain remains the most expensive transfer of all time.

In June he made his first appearance for Brazil since 2023 after rupturing his ACL and meniscus in his left knee.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anthony Nolan | 20 Nov 2026 23:59.

Werder Bremen will be battling to keep their unlikely European dream alive on Sunday, when they welcome Hamburger SV to the Weserstadion for a Bundesliga Nordderby.

Die Werderaner are hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out, while HSV are keen to pick up where they left off prior to the international break.

Daniel Thioune guided Werder to safety last term after taking the helm in early February, though his sights are set much higher this time around with his team sat in a strong position upon the league's return.

Nine matches into the campaign, Die Werderaner are sixth in the Bundesliga table, where their tally of 15 points has them two clear of seventh-placed Elversberg and just three shy of RB Leipzig in fourth.

Securing European football of any variety would be a major accomplishment for Thioune, who is currently in his first top-flight role as manager, not to mention that the club last appeared on the continental stage back in the 2010-11 Champions League group stage.

However, Werder signed off for the international break with a 1-0 defeat at Stuttgart on November 7, their second loss in three matches after a 3-2 beating by Borussia Dortmund in the DFB-Pokal in late October.

In fairness to the Green-Whites, they fought back from 2-0 down against BVB thanks to a brace from Niclas Fullkrug, only to lose out to a stoppage-time free kick by Marcel Sabitzer.

Additionally, a 2-0 victory over Hoffenheim between those defeats saw the hosts maintain their unbeaten streak on home turf this season, where they will hope to record a fourth win in five outings on Sunday.

Meanwhile, Merlin Polzin's Hamburger endured a dire start to the season, conceding 12 goals without reply in their first three Bundesliga games before firing back with a run of three consecutive triumphs.

It would be fair to say that HSV's term has been defined by streaks so far, alternating between trios of defeats and wins across all competitions, and the club will be hoping to stabilise after the international break.

Polzin's side were held to a 1-1 draw by Croatia's Hajduk Split in a friendly on November 15, following up a 3-1 success against Borussia Monchengladbach that helped to distance the team from the relegation zone in the German top flight.

That victory has left Hamburger 11th in the Bundesliga table with 12 points to their name - a total that puts them level with Eintracht Frankfurt, Hoffenheim and Stuttgart up to eighth - as well as five points clear of 16th-placed Union Berlin.

Earning another win on Sunday would be keeping with HSV's pattern this term, but after seeing the visitors lose four of their five away league matches in 2026-27, fans would be forgiven for harbouring doubts.

Werder Bremen form (all competitions):.

Hamburger SV form (all competitions):.

Werder will be without strikers Keke Topp (ACL) and Salim Musah (thigh) once again as they recover from long-term injuries, though the doubts about Marco Grull's fitness after he missed training with a calf issue will be a major concern for the team.

If Grull is sidelined on Sunday, then expect to see Niclas Fullkrug supported up top by Eren Dinkci, Chuki and Justin Njinmah.

Jens Stage and Skelly Alvero are also unavailable due to respective thigh and calf injuries, while question marks remain about the readiness of fellow midfielder Senne Lynen, who has been ill over the past week, though Youri Regeer and Ludovit Reis should be on hand to form Thioune's double pivot.

Elsewhere, the versatile Mitchell Weiser is a doubt with a thigh problem and left-back Moussa N'Diaye is recovering from a groin injury, so Arthur and Olivier Deman look set to start at full-back.

As for Hamburger, they are missing centre-back Jordan Torunarigha, who has been dealing with a hip issue, but Mario Vuskovic is likely to return after getting over a minor back injury.

The visitors are lighter in midfield than ideal, with all three of Albert Sambi Lokonga (calf), Bilal Nadir (thigh) and Nicolai Remberg (ACL) sidelined, so Martin Adeline could join Miro Muheim in the centre of the park, while Albert Gronbaek operates in the number 10 role.

Striker Yussuf Poulsen is also out with a calf injury, but Terem Moffi and Patson Daka will be ready to lead the line in a strike partnership on Sunday.

Werder Bremen possible starting lineup:.

Hein; Arthur, Friedl, Pieper, Deman; Regeer, Reis; Dinkci, Chuki, Njinmah; Fullkrug.

Hamburger SV possible starting lineup:.

Heuer; Capaldo, Omari, Bornauw; El Ouahdi, Adeline, Muheim, Moller Wolfe; Gronbaek; Moffi, Daka.

Werder have been exceptional on home turf this season, and they will be expecting to collect all three points once again, but the match is likely to be closer than otherwise if Grull remains sidelined.

By contrast, Hamburger have struggled on the road throughout 2026-27, and with four defeats in five away Bundesliga games so far, expect to see the visitors' pattern of results broken.

Industry observers note that manchester United transfer news: Red Devils captain Bruno Fernandes has turned down a second contract offer, according to a report from The Athletic covered by CaughtOffside. The 32-year-old is unhappy with both the proposed salary and the length of the deal, and the standoff lands with his current contract set to expire in June 2027.

The calendar adds pressure. In 50 days, Fernandes can open talks with foreign clubs, and Galatasaray have already been linked. United hold a 12-month extension option that stops him leaving for free, but triggering it only postpones the argument and keeps an unhappy captain in the dressing room.

Recent findings suggest that the refusal follows a bad few weeks. After a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes publicly criticised Michael Carrick’s tactics, and Carrick dropped him for the Bournemouth game. Carrick has since been sacked with United 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, so Mauricio Pochettino inherits the standoff alongside a team in trouble.

According to recent reports, his strengths are obvious. He set a Premier League record with 21 assists last season, delivers set pieces better than anyone at the club and opened this campaign with a hat-trick against Ipswich. His weaknesses are just as clear. At 32, the Portuguese international gives little protection when United lose the ball, and his shot selection can be wasteful.

Pochettino’s best sides pressed hard and ran through a creative number ten with two athletic midfielders behind him. Fernandes suits the creative role, but only if those two midfielders cover his space.

United should keep him, but on shorter terms than he wants. Nobody else in the squad creates chances at his rate, and a team sitting in the bottom three cannot replace that in January. A long, expensive deal for a player entering his mid-thirties would create a wage problem just as Pochettino tries to rebuild the midfield around younger runners.

Sources indicate that the sensible offer is a short contract with a raise tied to appearances and Champions League qualification. That respects his standing without committing United beyond the point where his legs start to fail.

If Fernandes still refuses, the board should trigger the extension and sell next summer. A sale with a year left on his deal will still bring a meaningful fee, whereas losing him for nothing in 2027 would waste the one asset United can sell on their own terms.

It has been revealed that arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all contacted Bournemouth about England midfielder Alex Scott, according to CaughtOffside, which cites The i Paper. Liverpool and Chelsea want to move in January, while Arsenal would rather wait until next summer. Bournemouth’s stance on selling the 23-year-old has softened, but the reported asking price is above £100m, and Scott turned down two contract offers over the summer.

The interest has clear reasons behind it. Andoni Iraola coached Scott at Bournemouth before taking over at Anfield in June, and Liverpool want to reunite them. Chelsea lost Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in a £125m deadline-day deal and had a reported £64m bid for Scott rejected earlier in the summer. Arsenal already have Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Zubimendi and Myles Lewis-Skelly, so CaughtOffside sees Chelsea or Liverpool as the more logical destinations for his playing time.

In a recent development, scott wins the ball, presses and carries it through midfield, and he started Bournemouth’s first five league games this season before a quadriceps injury on England duty in October kept him out for weeks. Fitness is the first concern, because knee problems have interrupted much of his time on the south coast. End product is the second. He has scored five league goals in 85 appearances since joining in 2023, so he will not solve a shortage of chances alone.

Sources indicate that not at £100m, and not as a January priority. Liverpool rank 18th for significant chances after ten league games, according to This Is Anfield, and Scott offers energy rather than creativity. The real gap sits beside Ryan Gravenberch, where Curtis Jones left in the summer, and nobody arrived to share the defensive work.

Scott could be the aggressive partner in Iraola’s double pivot, freeing Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz to play higher, yet that is a heavy fee for a player only just rebuilding match fitness, with Liverpool fourth and nine points behind Arsenal.

Chelsea’s case is simpler. The division’s biggest summer spenders lost their midfield engine and can justify the price more easily. Arsenal’s patience makes sense, since Rice, Guimaraes and Zubimendi leave no room for a £100m squad player. A Liverpool bid would only inflate the market Chelsea are already shaping. If Iraola wants a January signing, a specialist holding midfielder for far less money does more for the top-four push.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Towards the end of their lives, stars experience a drastic change in their structure as they swell and enter what is known as their giant phase. Because most stars are thought to host orbiting companions (such as planets, other stars or black holes), interesting interactions can happen as the giant host expands. The most striking of these occur when a companion star is engulfed by a giant: astronomers refer to this as the common-envelope phase1. Despite theoretical expectations that common envelopes should be widespread in stellar evolution, they have been extraordinarily difficult to observe. Writing in Nature, however, Karambelkar et al.2 report the first direct detection of a star inside a giant star.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Zeki Çelik was withdrawn from Türkiye's starting line-up in Bordeaux after feeling tightness in the same left thigh muscle he injured in October.
  • In a recent development, zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux.
  • Sources indicate that an Emirhan Topçu own goal and a goal from Eli Junior Kroupi put France ahead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Zeki Çelik was withdrawn from Türkiye's starting line-up in Bordeaux after feeling tightness in the same left thigh muscle he injured in October. With Pierre Kalulu already sidelined, Juventus face tests that could leave them without both main right-sided defenders for Venezia and Omonia.

In a recent development, zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux. The Juventus full-back was named in Türkiye’s starting line-up for Sunday’s Nations League match against France. His left hamstring tightened up as he went through the warm-up. He was taken out of the matchday squad as a precaution. Barış Alper Yılmaz started in his place.

Sources indicate that an Emirhan Topçu own goal and a goal from Eli Junior Kroupi put France ahead. Abdülkerim Bardakcı scored a late reply for Türkiye. The result left France top of Nations League Group A1 with 13 points. They are through to the quarter-finals, which are due next March.

Çelik now returns to Turin for tests at J|Medical. Those results will decide how Juventus line up at the back after the international break.

The location is what worries Juventus. Çelik was substituted at half-time in the 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes. His scans took place on the morning of Friday 23 October. He began a rehabilitation programme straight away and was expected back after the November break.

Industry observers note that tuttosport counted him among Spalletti’s first returning players, alongside Vicario and Gatti. The paper placed the Bordeaux problem in the biceps femoris of his left thigh. That is the same area as the October injury.

Çelik had only just returned after weeks out. That is why the warm-up incident has raised fears of a relapse. No diagnosis has yet been confirmed.

According to recent reports, juventus were already without Pierre Kalulu. He picked up the injury in the game against Fiorentina. He began treatment and was withdrawn from the France squad. Sky Sport Italia expected him to be out for about three weeks. That would rule him out of both the Venezia and Omonia matches.

If Çelik’s problem proves to be a relapse, Spalletti could be without both of his main right-sided defenders for those two games. The schedule offers little room for recovery. The Omonia match is the second of four games in 12 days.

It has been revealed that the league position adds pressure. After 11 rounds Juventus are seventh in Serie A with 18 points. Their record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats.

Sources indicate that venezia visit Turin first, at 12:30 on 22 November in round 12 of Serie A. Omonia then come to the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November in the Europa League league phase.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, so much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

"It's PETULANT from Cole Palmer...you have to take it on the chin" Jamie Redknapp and Daniel Sturridge react to Cole Palmer's pair of yellow cards 🟥 https://t.co/Voxoo3Ea7V.

Palmer was just about the only Chelsea player not to have been sent off last season, but it seems that Alonso has not yet managed to deal with the club’s disciplinary problem.

In a recent development, jordan Henderson had given Palmer a talking to at the end of the win at Everton in which the forward was booked. But he evidently did not heed the advice or the words of his manager.

Alonso had said he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

In between Palmer’s two bookings, Penders suffered his own moment of madness with a bizarre own goal on his league debut for Chelsea. The Belgian was standing in for Emi Martinez, who watched in disbelief from the home dug-out after undergoing surgery on his jaw.

Recent findings suggest that fernandes sent in a corner that Jan Paul van Hecke challenged for. Penders looked like the easy winner in that contest, but he got his punch horribly wrong and the ball spun backwards and over the goalline.

According to recent reports, "Just look what it means!" A glorious solo run and finish from Mathys Tel! 🤩 https://t.co/Qg7WMFNlwQ.

In a recent development, tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi celebrated wildly with his staff. The two benches had clashed and De Zerbi had been booked after Palmer’s first yellow card that the Italian felt should have been a red. But De Zerbi will not care about that now, with Tottenham’s season finally up and running thanks to successive league wins against Coventry City and Chelsea.

"They were brilliant Spurs, they really were" Gary Neville's immediate reaction to Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham 🗣️ https://t.co/QWhi7Blmfz.

Tottenham should really have been ahead in the first half. De Zerbi revealed before the game that Dominic Solanke had dropped down to the substitutes’ bench because the striker “felt fatigue” after the victory over Coventry.

With Solanke resting up on the bench until the 65th minute, De Zerbi moved Omar Marmoush, who had scored his first Spurs goal against Coventry, into the middle and brought in Tel on the left.

In a recent development, tel was involved in the 29th-minute move that should have resulted in the opening goal for Marmoush. The Frenchman played a one-two with Andy Robertson and the Scotsman picked out Marmoush with a low cross. But, six yards out and with time to pick his spot, the former Manchester City man allowed Penders to make a save.

The missed Marmoush chance was the first time Penders had been called into action. At the other end, Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky made unnecessary work for himself.

In a recent development, kinsky played a bad pass straight to Pedro Neto. The ball was worked to Henderson, but Kinsky recovered to make a save and then stopped the follow-up from Neto. The offside flag then went up, but it was unclear whether it would have spared Kinsky on both occasions had Chelsea scored.

It was not the first time Kinsky had handed possession back to Chelsea in a dangerous area, although the 23-year-old had also made a good save to palm away a curling effort from Palmer. That came after Fernandes had the ball pinched from him far too easily.

Neto was Chelsea’s most dangerous player, but it was the wrong call by Alonso to leave Danny Welbeck on the bench, with João Pedro out injured, and he was too slow to change things. Leaving it until the 88th minute, when the game had already been killed by Tel, to send on the striker was a clear error.

Storm Boelo created wet-and-wild conditions on the Stamford Bridge pitch, while there were still remnants of Storm Austen, or should that be Storm Austin, on the home bench.

Chelsea set-piece coach Austin MacPhee let out an incredibly loud “for f---’s sake” when one corner routine went wrong. Nobody could hear what he was shouting over the Tottenham celebrations when Penders scored his own goal, but it would almost certainly have started with “f” again.

James Maddison had been a doubt before the game after missing training during the week and it only took four minutes of the second half for him to signal to De Zerbi that he needed to come off.

Maddison had scored a brilliant goal on his first league start in 18 months against Coventry, but he had to be replaced by former Chelsea midfielder Gallagher at Stamford Bridge.

James Maddison is forced off with an injury and is replaced by Conor Gallagher, who receives a mixed reception from his former fans 🔃 https://t.co/GSeXQQ3eoa.

The Chelsea fans predictably booed Gallagher, a graduate of the club’s academy who at times even stood in as captain. The foul on Gallagher that earned Palmer his marching orders silenced the jeers and the Chelsea fans’ boos only returned at the final whistle for their own players.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has told Cole Palmer he must learn from his red card that contributed to his team’s London derby defeat by Tottenham Hotspur.

Industry observers note that tottenham head coach Roberto De Zerbi insisted Palmer should have seen red for shoving his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes. But, having got off with a yellow card, the Chelsea midfielder then fouled substitute Conor Gallagher.

It has been revealed that “I haven’t seen them [the yellow cards] on TV, but as far as I have been told, he [the referee] probably got it right,” Alonso stated. “So, for sure for Cole, but for everyone. We think [up until] now we haven’t received any red cards [this season] and we need to continue that way because we need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments, when you have conceded 1-0, there was still 15-20 minutes to go, so we have to be calm. I need to check the action to talk with Cole, but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”.

Asked if he thought Palmer should have been sent off for the first yellow card, De Zerbi, who was booked for his protests, replied: “Yep.”.

Jordan Henderson had spoken to Palmer at the end of the previous week’s victory over Everton in which the forward could also have been booked for a second time and sent off.

But Alonso claimed he does not have any wider concerns about Palmer’s character. He said: “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a [wider] concern. I think that Cole when he is focused on the game, when he is enjoying and today after the 1-0, it is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature and for everyone.”.

De Zerbi hailed his side’s character and claimed that Tottenham have “suffered enough” after two 17th-placed finishes and a slow start to the season until successive victories over Coventry City and Chelsea.

Recent findings suggest that “We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough,” De Zerbi remarked. “Changing the spirit of the group, changing the performance of the players, especially the more fragile players, maybe the younger players. We played very well. Great individual performances, great collective performance because we played very well. And then we put something different than Tottenham, I think, in the last period. Different attitude, different relationships with the players, different group.”.

Chelsea were without João Pedro because of an injury and Alonso is waiting to find out how long the striker will be out.

“We don’t know yet because he has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “So he felt it yesterday [Friday] and we need to wait probably until tomorrow [Sunday] to do the test and to know the whole situation and the whole seriousness of the injury. We will know soon enough.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met. Chelsea sent the 22-year-old to Villa Park on a season-long loan in July, with a reported £43m obligation to buy next summer. Neither club has revealed the trigger, and reports link it to appearances.

The numbers explain the concern. FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances. Football Insider claims Villa are prepared to back out of the deal if his form doesn’t improve.

Garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed. His pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders earned a £40m move from Manchester United in 2025. The weakness is end product, and it followed him to London with eight goals in 43 games for Chelsea, only one of them in 24 Premier League appearances. Unai Emery left him out of the squad for the Manchester United game.

Chelsea have no obvious use for him either. Xabi Alonso told him in July that regular football wasn’t guaranteed, and the 3-4-2-1 Alonso favours uses Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind João Pedro, with Pedro Neto and Estêvão competing for the wide roles.

FotMob values him at about €29m (roughly £25m), far below the €71m peak recorded in August 2024, and Manchester United are reportedly entitled to 10 per cent of any future fee. If the clause isn’t triggered, he returns in July 2027 on a contract running to 2032.

Yes, and soon. Chelsea built the deal to protect £43m, but the clause relies on appearances from a manager who isn’t picking him, so the price drops with every unused substitution. The sporting case for a return is thin. Alonso’s system asks wide players to defend as wing-backs, while Garnacho’s value lies in isolating a full-back, and the £117m Rogers signing already covers the left-sided attacking role.

Industry observers note that A mid-£20m sale, even after United’s cut, would still return more than half of the £40m Chelsea paid and clear a contract running to 2032. Chelsea should open talks with Villa in January about a lower fixed fee, or line up other buyers for the summer. A clause that depends on a manager picking a player he has benched was never a safe way to protect £43m.

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister, according to @tribuna_ftbl, with his current deal running until June 2028. The report arrives days after his father, Carlos, told ESPN that no discussions had started, although he hinted at news before the end of the year.

It also reverses the summer, when the club extended Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai but made no offer to the 27-year-old, something Mac Allister revealed in September while admitting he had stayed despite chances to leave.

Recent findings suggest that his form explains the change. After a poor 2025/26 under Arne Slot, he has become Andoni Iraola’s first-choice midfielder alongside Szoboszlai, pushing Gravenberch to the bench. He has scored once in the Premier League and three times in the Champions League, including the winner against Atlético Madrid, and holds a 7.29 FotMob average rating across 758 league minutes. Liverpool sit fourth.

FotMob places him in the 88th percentile among midfielders for shot attempts, and he has said the man-to-man system suits him because it demands less communication than Slot’s approach. His weaknesses are just as clear.

It has been revealed that his defensive contributions (45th percentile) and aerial duels (46th) sit below the midfield average, and pundit David Lynch has questioned whether his legs have gone in Iraola’s 4-4-2, where two central midfielders cover huge areas. He has also collected four league yellow cards already.

Sources indicate that yes, but not on the terms his summer rebound might demand. Ten league games of good form do not cancel a season in which he looked off the pace, so Liverpool should offer around three years, with wages pitched below the bumper deals Gravenberch and Szoboszlai signed.

The timing still makes sense. With 18 months left, he enters the final year next summer, when Liverpool would face either a discounted sale or a free departure. His FotMob valuation of €66m has almost halved from the €130m peak of September 2025, so selling now would lock in the lowest price.

Iraola also needs a controller to sit beside Szoboszlai’s runs, and no one in the squad does that better. The caveat is that Mac Allister turns 28 next month, so Liverpool must pair him with a quicker partner next summer rather than treat his renewal as the end of the midfield rebuild.

Brest arrive on the back of consecutive victories, leaving the visitors well placed to edge a closely contested encounter and extend their impressive record at Stade de la Meinau.

One of football’s largest financial lenders abandoned a planned £1.5billion loan to Manchester City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

The decision by US private capital group Apollo Global Management is the latest evidence that the money markets deem City a financial risk, as the club prepare an appeal against their conviction on the vast majority of 115 Premier League charges of inflating income through sham contracts.

Industry observers note that it was reported by Bloomberg last week that a German lender, Oldenburgische Landesbank (OL), had pulled out of a deal that would have let Brazilian top-flight side Palmeiras take a large upfront payment against instalments City are due to pay them for midfielder Allan Elias, signed this summer for £32million with £2m add-ons. That bank views City as a reputational and financial risk.

The Financial Times reported on Thursday that Apollo was in the final stages of negotiating the loan to City Football Group (CFG) in September, when the deal collapsed after the ruling that they artificially inflated their financial position to the tune of more than £900m over nine years.

It has been revealed that city owner Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan injected £100m into the club in the month after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi. Sheikh Mansour, who has only been present at one City home game since Abu Dhabi bought the club in 2008, has made no public comment on the club’s conviction, which delivers huge reputational damage to his image-conscious country.

There are signs that football is preparing for a strong legal attack from Abu Dhabi if City lose their appeal. Premier League clubs have voted to cover legal expenses for the organisation's five board directors in the event of sponsors Etihad and Etisalat suing them, it was also unveiled on Thursday. Legal indemnity will be in place for CEO Richard Masters, chair Alison Brittain and three other non-executive directors.

US private capital group Apollo Global Management abandoned a £1.5billion loan to Man City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

City owner Sheikh Mansou injected £100m into the club after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi.

But the refusal of credit by Apollo, which has loaned £80m to Premier League football club Nottingham Forest and has a minority stake in Championship side Wrexham, demonstrates that the capital markets think City are imperilled, with the appeal process by no means straightforward.

If an appeal failed, City could seek a judicial review of the commission's findings at the High Court. But to do so, they would need to demonstrate that the Premier League acted outside its powers or reached a conclusion which no reasonable authority could have reached. City would need the High Court’s permission to make a judicial review application and the bar is high.

Financial analyst Paul Quinn wrote on The Esk website that Apollo’s matter had been with City, not Abu Dhabi itself. Three weeks ago, Apollo agreed to take a minority stake in Mubadala Capital, the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund chaired by Sheikh Mansour and run by City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. Apollo and City have not commented.

It has been revealed that quinn noted that CFG needed the money because it was not self-funding, despite City’s financial strength. CFG’s pre-tax loss widened from £122.2m to £292.3m in the last financial year. City produced £694.1m of CFG’s £888m group revenue and ran up a £9m loss.

Bayern Munich have announced England captain Harry Kane will be out for a "few months" after he sustained an ankle injury in the 1-1 draw against FC Koln.

After netting in England's 3-2 win over Spain on Sunday, Kane returned to action for Bayern in Friday's Bundesliga meeting with Koln at the Allianz Arena.

Kane was named in the starting lineup as Vincent Kompany made his return to the touchline for the first time since he collapsed while watching Bayern's second team train.

As it proved, Bayern could not have got off to a worse start as Mikey Moore put Koln in front, shortly before Kane was forced off in the 20th minute.

The Ballon d'Or winner picked up the injury in the 15th minute when he attempted to reach Michael Olise's cross.

However, Koln full-back Joel Schmied slid in to beat Kane to the ball, although he caught the Bayern star in the process.

The 33-year-old hobbled on for a few minutes before he eventually went to ground to receive treatment.

Unable to continue, Kane was replaced by Tom Bischof, who provided the assist for Nathaniel Brown to equalise with what proved to be the final goal of the game.

Bayern also lost Michael Olise to injury at the half-time interval, which compounded a disappointing evening for the reigning Bundesliga champions.

The Bavarians have since provided a swift but pessimistic patch on Kane's injury status.

According to recent reports, the statement read: "Harry Kane suffered a torn syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle during FC Bayern's Bundesliga home match against 1. FC Köln on Friday evening.

According to recent reports, "This was confirmed by an examination conducted by FC Bayern's medical department. The 33-year-old will therefore be sidelined for the next few months.".

Bayern also revealed Olise will "receive treatment in the coming days" after sustaining a foot problem.

In line with Bayern's "few months" timeframe, Florian Plettenberg reports that Kane will be out for at least three months with the ankle problem.

However, there is an understandable caution in putting an exact timeframe on his recovery at this early stage.

Using the early three-month prediction as a guideline, Kane will miss Bayern's final four Champions League league phase matches against Lille, Slavia Prague, Manchester United and Real Betis.

Kane would also be a doubt to feature in the knockout phase playoffs if Bayern fail to secure a top-eight finish in the league phase.

In regard to the Bundesliga, he could miss the next 12 matchdays if he is out until at least February 20.

Meanwhile, England boss Thomas Tuchel will be nervously waiting to find out the exact timeframe for Kane's rehabilitation process.

If it is around three months, Kane would be back in time for England's UEFA Nations League quarter-final clash against Norway.

But if he needs longer to recover, England's greatest goalscorer would be in a race to prove his fitness in time for the two-legged clash.

The Three Lions will travel to Norway on March 27 before hosting the second leg a few days later.

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Industry observers note that anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola said. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”.

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP.

Liverpool’s lead was secured with an element of good fortune but, equally, the tenacity of Ronald Araújo and Wirtz was instrumental in pressing Brighton back to the point that they were panicking; Wirtz’s shot, deflected off Pascal Gross past Bart Verbruggen, compounded it all.

Sources indicate that “I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two massive chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”.

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an notable moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR.

Remarkably, this was the first time Liverpool had scored in the first half at Anfield in a Premier League fixture since May 9 and, with that momentum, it led to one of those periods when they started attacking in waves and carried the crowd with them.

What they needed was a second goal to arrive quite quickly and that is what happened when Barcola won possession, scuttled forward and played a perfectly weighted bobbling ball into Isak’s path; the Swede did the rest, calmly finishing from eight yards.

According to recent reports, everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

Alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb.

“The performance was really good,” noted Isak, the quiet assassin. “We were really solid against a really good team. The first half is what we really want to be about. It was about intensity, winning balls and countering.”.

Brighton, as much as Hürzeler protested, could not properly recover, though this is no criticism. They remain committed to attack, they struck the frame of the goal when Ayari tried to punish an Alisson Becker mistake and the desire to keep pushing ensured Liverpool could never relax.

What Liverpool had going for them this time, however, was an intensity to preserve a clean sheet and nobody embodied the indefatigability more than Araújo, the Uruguay international whose loan from Barcelona is looking an increasingly shrewd piece of business.

Two moments stood out: one thunderous tackle on substitute Malick Yalcouyé in front of the Main Stand that had the locals roaring their approval, another in the first half when he was on the floor but still managed to head away to thwart Maxim De Cuyper.

Recent findings suggest that they remember those moments as much as the stardust that Barcola and Isak provide. Put it all together and it might just be a launchpad for Iraola.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Liverpool and Brighton & Hove Albion at Anfield.

Liverpool are on a three-game winning run in all competitions, and came from two goals behind in their previous outing in the Champions League on Tuesday, earning an enthralling 4-3 victory over Villarreal. Last weekend, Andoni Iraola’s men also initially fell behind against Brentford in the Premier League, but netted two second-half goals through Daniel Munoz and Alexander Isak to win 2-1 as their opponents finished with nine men.

In a recent development, in his programme notes, Liverpool boss Iraola was excited about the prospect of a second game in a week at home. “As someone who believes every single opportunity we have to play a game at this stadium and in front of our supporters is a privilege, I also feel very passionately that this is a period that we should continue to embrace,” he mentioned.

“It is also a spell in which we will carry on being tested because the quality of the opposition dictates that there is no chance of anything else. Villarreal pushed us all the way in midweek and everything about the way Brighton have played so far this season tells us that it would be foolish to expect anything but the same today.”.

It has been revealed that brighton have emerged as one of the surprise packages of the Premier League season thanks to their blistering start. Fabian Hurzeler’s side sit third in the table, having scored a whopping 23 goals in their opening seven games, while conceding just five. On Thursday, Brighton were unexpectedly held to a 0-0 draw by Czech outfit Jablonec, ending a run of six straight victories in all competitions. Nevertheless, they’re unbeaten since their 4-3 league loss to Chelsea back on August 30.

Recent findings suggest that defender Ferdi Kadioglu believes his team’s energy and fitness has played a huge role in their eye-catching form. “If you want to play how we play, you have to be very fit,” he remarked. “We were already fit last season, but I think it’s more that now everyone really understands what we need to do to win matches. That’s really clear this season, and everyone is doing it. Everyone is really focused on their task and doing it very well so far.”.

Despite some mistakes this early in the season, Mancini remains a key figure in Gasperini’s defense. The coach continues to focus on the center-back, whom he knows well from his time at Atalanta.

According to Calciomercato.it, Mancini’s name is still on Inter’s list for the next transfer window.

Chivu needs defensive reinforcements, especially given the possible departures of Bisseck and Stones.
